text:
Alex: Heads-up — eu-west rack42 is showing a tail-latency spike since 12:10UTC, graph looks like an egress microburst. A few dedicated tenants got higher p95, shared tenants worse. Anyone digging?
Mira: On it, linking grafana + logs. query I'll run: `sum(rate(nic_tx_bytes[1m])) by (host)` and look for outliers.
TJ: My suspicion: one tenant doing large sampling/beam-search batches that saturate PCIe or NIC queues. Check `pci_util` + `tx_queue_len` on those hosts.
Alex: quick extract from host-42-11: `nic_tx_pkts` jumped 8x, pcie_util ~ 92% for 30s, `ksoftirq` spikes.
InfraBot: [alert] net-queue-fullness@rack42 host-42-11 threshold breached (severity: medium). Auto-throttle not triggered because tenant is in dedicated-pool.
Samir: If it's a dedicated tenant, our default is to not auto-throttle. Proposal: soft-quarantine mode — move offending tenant to ephemeral hot-pool and apply egress-shaper for 10m while we root cause. Tradeoff: burst capacity + cost. Thoughts?
Mira: +1 for soft-quarantine. Can we do a non-disruptive handoff? prefer `evict --soft` that keeps KV cache warm.
TJ: Also add temporary NIC Cgroup shaping so other tenants don't see queue buildup. Config snippet: ```yaml
egress_shaper:
  tenant: acme-bigjob
  max_bandwidth_mb: 250
  burst_ms: 200
  mode: soft
```
Alex: Running soft-evict now: `./tools/evict-tenant --tenant=acme-bigjob --mode=soft --target=hot-pool-eu2`
Alex: evict tool output: "handoff:start -> warming KV cache on hot-pool-eu2; attach egress-shaper"
Samir: I'll apply NIC cgroup via ops-runbook: `opsctl shaper apply --host host-42-11 --cfg /tmp/acme-shaper.yaml`
Mira: After handoff p95 on rack42 dropped from 310ms -> 78ms in 3m. Nice. Need to track cost delta for customer: moving to hot-pool used 0.4 GPU-hrs extra in first 10m.
TJ: Root cause follow-ups: was this a new model rollout (bigger token lengths) or an unbounded beam width? check task histograms for seq_len and batch_size.
Alex: Owner says they rolled a sampling change ~11:50UTC increasing beam_size=16 -> 64. That matches.
Samir: For long-term: propose tenant-level soft throttles for dedicated pools (config flag) + automatic egress-credit deduction and billing note. Ping finance for cost impact.
Mira: Agree. Also adding a scheduler tweak: if NIC tx saturation > 80% for >20s, and host in dedicated pool, trigger soft-quarantine policy (no immediate hard eviction).
InfraBot: Created ticket INFRA-1729 to track follow-up (auto-throttle for dedicated tenants + billing hook).
TJ: Ok. Let's keep the handoff active for 30m, monitor, then revert if stable. Postmortem if this repeats.
Alex: Thanks all — closing loop in 30m unless we see regressions :thumbsup:
